Package net.sourceforge.plantuml.klimt

Enum Class UShapeKind

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Enum<UShapeKind>
net.sourceforge.plantuml.klimt.UShapeKind
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Comparable<UShapeKind>, Constable
public enum UShapeKind extends Enum<UShapeKind>
The closed set of UShape kinds a UDriver can be registered for, and the reason an AbstractUGraphic can keep its drivers in a plain array rather than a map: the kind is a small dense index, so a lookup is drivers[kind.ordinal()]. Membership here is exactly "some driver, in some output format, knows how to draw this" -- the thirteen classes every UGraphic implementation registers between them. It is not the set of all UShape implementations: most of those are containers or decorations that never reach AbstractUGraphic#draw as themselves. Those keep UNKNOWN, which no driver is ever registered under, so asking for one still finds an empty slot and fails exactly as an unregistered class did before. Each constant names the class it stands for, so this enum is the single place that pairs the two; UShape.getShapeKind()'s overrides are checked against it by every diagram that renders, since a shape returning the wrong kind would find the wrong driver (or none) the first time it is drawn.
